title: Tankers Still Afloat
summary:
Tankers Still Afloat
The shipping markets tend to ebb and flow with the health and cycles of the world economy and trade. While it is sometimes difficult to determine the root causes of the bursts in the market, a downward correction in freight rates can be felt quickly especially if there is a surplus of tonnage. Sudden changes in demand and consumption patterns can convert a well supplied market into one with a capacity glut to the detriment of shipowners.

children.title: Comparitive Freight Rates
children.summary: It appears that dry bulk shipping has fallen victim to a few of the classic symptoms of a market bubble. Demand for dry bulk commodities grew creating congestion at ports with insufficient infrastructure.

children.title: Key Driving Factors
children.summary: Demand for oil continues to grow. Although demand figures have been revised downward recently due to the slowing global economy, analysts still expect growth in consumption to be between 300,000 to 600,000 barrels per day next year.
